Your Project Description (max 2000 chara: Butterfly Dance explores how personal birthday information can be encrypted through cryptography and then transformed into visual work through visual rules and generative code. I really like butterflies, so I chose the butterfly as the main visual element. I divided the butterfly into five variables: upper wings, lower wings, body, antennae, and color, and used numerical codes to control these different visual features. The project began with a “birthday cryptography” system: each person’s birthday is converted into a set of numbers, and these numbers determine the different forms of the butterfly. As a result, each person can enter their birthday and generate a butterfly of their own.

Your Project Description (max 2000 chara:
Between Us is a visual system for translating social interactions into visual systems. The project began by asking whether something as subjective as communication could be reduced to a set of rules. I identified four variables within an interaction: understanding, engagement, avoidance, and success, and used them to control the direction, distance, movement, and eventual meeting point of lines traveling between two individuals.

Early experiments isolated these interactions one at a time. Two circles represented two people, while animated lines moved toward one another. Depending on the conditions assigned to the interaction, the lines could meet, overlap, pass one another, or move in different directions. Randomness was built into the system so that similar conditions could produce related, but never identical, outcomes.

As the project developed, I became more interested in what happened when these individual exchanges accumulated in a specific place over a set period of time, as a way to archive a social gathering. The final iteration records multiple interactions occurring within the same space and period of time. Each colored circle represents an individual, with the number of lines emerging from it determined by how many interactions that person had. Some become highly connected, while others remain more isolated. Each trajectory retains the variables of the original system, while the dotted lines were added to represent the "missed opportunity" of an interaction -- how much understanding was lost, how much avoidance can redirect one's path, and the visual space that's left as a result.

Rather than trying to objectively measure human communication, the system uses code to reduce highly complex and subjective human patterns into simplified forms.

Your Project Description (max 2000 chara:
This system models the physical assembly and the many possibilities of studio ceramics through visual rules. Each vessel is assembled along a central axis from three stacked components - a base, midsection, and neck - selected from randomized geometric shapes and bounded sizes, ensuring the base remains the structural foundation. 

Surface appearances translate simulated physical and atmospheric conditions: clay body determines opacity (40% Porcelain, 70% Stoneware, 100% Terracotta), while glaze chemistry responds to kiln oxygen levels. Cobalt produces a constant deep blue, Copper shifts from an oxidized green-turquoise gradient to a reduced deep red, and Iron Oxide transforms from a warm yellow-brown gradient to charcoal. 

By combining and controlling the variables within this system, across 32 geometric profiles, 18 material states, and continuous component scaling, the system generates infinite unique, visually readable ceramic pots that can be helpful to the ceramicist when reading the appearance.

Your Project Name: A week Daily Sleep Quality Data
Your Project Description (max 2000 chara:
7Days is an algorithmic data translation system that transforms personal, tracked sleep logs from Monday through Sunday into an expressive visual cipher. Developed through an integrated workflow bridging computational code in p5.js and Adobe Illustrator, the system treats daily bio metric quality as dynamic parameters rather than passive static records.

Moving beyond conventional health charts that flatten personal metrics, 7Days reclaims bio metric tracking as an active generator of form, texture, and structural meaning. Operating within p5.js, the system maps sleep metrics—including total duration, REM/deep sleep ratios, heart rate variability (HRV), and wake frequencies—to geometric parameters: deep sleep drives smooth, low-frequency wave functions, REM generates high-frequency node clusters, frequent awakenings introduce sharp spatial noise and fractures, and HRV governs the organic fluidity of the vector field.

The rendered SVG geometry is subsequently imported into Adobe Illustrator for vector refinement, where paths are enhanced with custom variable-width brushes, precision alignment, and chromatic hierarchy, deep indigo's represent restorative deep sleep, soft purples denote REM cycles, and high-contrast neon accents mark sleep interruptions. Arranged sequentially across a master seven-day grid, the final piece translates intimate biological rhythms into a cohesive weekly narrative that seamlessly bridges data art and computational design.
File 1 description: The system programmatically evaluates sleep quality and duration based on input variables. Each geometric cipher functions as a clock face, where the dashed contour outlines the exact time and duration of sleep.
File 2 description: I used if and else if statements to dynamically control the visual output based on daily sleep quality.
File 3 description: In p5.js, the design rules dynamically convert sleep logs into visual geometry, sleep deficit triggers push(), rotate(), and vertex() to build 90-degree rotated orange polygons (Need More Sleep), overlaid with line() vectors radiating outward to create sharp spike-like tension.
Anyone's work inspired you at the open c: Seeing my peers' work during the open critique was genuinely inspiring. It opened my eyes to how differently people can interpret and translate personal data into visual art. I was particularly impressed by the diverse color choices, creative algorithms in p5.js, and unique storytelling approaches everyone used to bridge code and graphic design. It challenged me to think more deeply about how I structure my own generative systems and how to refine the dialogue between raw data and visual poetry.

This project explores a visual translation system that encodes language into form. Starting from five primary shapes extracted from descriptive words, the visual elements were algorithmically transformed through a set of grammatical rules based on Richard Serra’s action verbs—stretching, splitting, bending, and systematizing.
Rather than displaying text directly, the project delays comprehension and treats typography and form as an encrypted diagnostic language. Ultimately, these forms were brought together to create a large-scale clinical poster that explores and maps out the anatomy of an alien body.
